look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · Non-prickly herb with alternate simple oval leaves, small white five-lobed stars, and round berries green when immature, purplish-black or sometimes greenish when mature. DON'T call it from black berries: check yellow anther length (~2–2.5 mm), relatively THICK flower/fruit stalks, and (if a verified specimen) the larger seeds and typically NO hard stone cells in North American fruits. Short anthers point toward S. americanum/emulans; longer rounded calyx lobes and uneven flower branches suggest S. interius. Introduced in Texas.

project_inclusion.range_basis: FNA: Solanum nigrum introduced and recorded in Texas; POWO accepted Eurasian-native species. Not presumed native to Hays County.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Solanaceae flowers typically fused five-part corolla and five stamens, superior ovary maturing into a many-seeded berry.
morphology_keys.habit: Unarmed annual or short-lived perennial, sprawling/erect, often to ~1 m, stems glabrous to pubescent, a disturbance-associated plant.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate simple petiolate ovate leaves, entire to coarsely toothed, often 3.5–7 cm long. Variable and not enough for species ID.
morphology_keys.flower: Small white five-pointed corolla, typically 1–1.5 cm across, yellow slender anthers ~2–2.5 mm according to FNA, flowering in short unbranched or forked racemelike clusters. Flower photo has no scale; don't claim photographed exact measurement.
morphology_keys.fruit: Globose ~5–10 mm berries dull to slightly shiny purple-black or green-yellowish at maturity, small calyx spreads to reflexes in fruit. Thickish peduncles and pedicels compared with native North American black nightshades. In North American S. nigrum fruit, stone cells absent—requires specialized safely handled specimen to verify, not photo proof.
morphology_keys.habitat: Disturbed areas, irrigated fields, roadsides and similar waste places; introduced in Texas according to Flora of North America.
morphology_keys.management: Treat as nonnative comparison plant; exact ID needed for management. Do NOT suggest berries edible from visual ID; unripe fruit and foliage may contain toxic glycoalkaloids.
crew_field_sequence: 1 · Check for prickles; no prickles plus white star flowers and round berries suggests MORELLOID group.
2 · Flower macro with ruler: anthers about 2–2.5 mm in S. nigrum; shorter in S. americanum and S. emulans.
3 · Check racemelike clusters and fruiting pedicel thickness, not simply fruit color.
4 · Mature berries can be dark OR greenish; photograph berry calyx and pedicel from side.
5 · If exact science ID is needed, compare seed size and hard stone cells under trained supervision: in North America S. nigrum fruits typically lack them.
6 · If only black fruit without flower structure is visible, label Solanum morelloid group until a measured photo and comparison are available.

field_terms.anther: Pollen-bearing yellow tip of a stamen; macro ruler helps separate anther lengths.
field_terms.peduncle: Shared stalk supporting an entire flower or fruit cluster; thicker in S. nigrum than many native black nightshades.
field_terms.sclerotic granule: Small hardened stone cell in fruit, not a seed; presence/absence is advanced dissection trait, not visible on intact fruit.
field_terms.calyx: Five green sepals at berry base; orientation matters but overlaps species.

morphology_keys.comparison_training: FNA's most practical S. nigrum confirmation among American morelloids combines thicker peduncles/pedicels, larger seeds, and absence of stone cells in North American fruit. The first photo does NOT prove those internal traits.

field_matrix.flower: White five-lobed corolla; yellow anthers ~2–2.5 mm
field_matrix.berries: Usually dull/slightly glossy purple-black or sometimes mature greenish, ~5–10 mm
field_matrix.seeds: Relatively large ~1.8–2 mm; North American berries usually NO stone cells
field_matrix.quick_rule: Thicker peduncle/pedicel + longer anthers + large seeds + no stone cells (North American material).

field_matrix.seeds: Typically smaller; fruit stone cells vary
field_matrix.quick_rule: SHORT anthers with tiny backward-curling ripe calyx.

field_matrix.flower: Shorter anthers and relatively longer free filaments
field_matrix.berries: Dull to mildly glossy dark fruit
field_matrix.quick_rule: Short anthers + appressed calyx + pedicel drops with berry.

field_matrix.seeds: Smaller seeds and often many stone cells
field_matrix.quick_rule: Anthers alone overlap; fruit dissection and multiple traits needed.
UNEVEN branching flower cluster + rounded-tip long calyx + larger fruit.

not_reliable_alone: Leaf shape, as different morelloids overlap
Fruit maturity judged solely from color
Absence of stone cells from a whole-fruit photo

visual_comparison.title: European black nightshade — compare anthers, fruit stalk thickness and stone cells
visual_comparison.subtitle: Genuine attributed Commons photographs showing flower/fruit roles. Internal stone cells require specimen examination; none of the photo arrows claim them.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: Longer anthers and THICKER fruiting stalks than American black nightshade. North American ripe berries usually lack the stone cells of several similar species.

field_photo_quickcheck.recognition: European nonnative black nightshade: white five-lobed flowers, small black or greenish berries, relatively thick peduncles and typically ~2–2.5 mm anthers. Confident ID uses combined traits.
what_to_photograph: Flower front and side with mm anther scale
Flower/fruit cluster stalk compared with adjacent morelloid
Whole branch with both green and ripe berries
Mature berry with calyx orientation clearly visible
Advanced: safely prepared seed size and berry stone-cell examination
missing: Measured 2–2.5 mm anther macro with ruler; current flower photo has no scale.
Voucher-controlled North American berry dissection for stone-cell trait; photos cannot prove absence.
